doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

title: Spiritual roots of Afro-Cuban music and respect for it
summary: Bunnett discusses playing music from a religious context without being a practitioner, informing herself through musicians around her.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did you run into a situation where you learned that some of this music I’m playing has a spiritual connection to it and this feeling like I should know about this and maybe I should be more careful with it?

Absolutely. I know exactly what you’re saying and that has hit me many times because it is so, you know this word we use expropriation etcetera, that you can be involved but not understand the deeper meaning of what it’s about and that it could come off as disrespectful or misinterpreted or any number of things. I guess in the case of that, because I guess you’re talking about the Afro-Cuban music because a lot of the music is from a very deep spiritual religious context. I guess I look at the musicians around me to inform me, you know, if there’s some—to inform me and also to inform myself, to be inquisitive and interested enough to go deeper into what I am trying to perform. I mean it’s a tricky question because I play, you know I have done a lot of work with the Afro- Cuban chants and, you know arranging the music that I’m hearing, and that music is for spiritual practice and the history, you know goes back hundreds of years. And at the same time I’m not a practitioner of Santeria or Afro-Cuban music but the melodies are so beautiful and the rhythms are — you know it’s so open for improvising and, you know, it’s coming from the same root of course as jazz music. So I just, you know I try and inform myself as much as possible and of course be surrounded by the other musicians that will, you know, I’ve often found when I have been performing that sometimes the guys are like so, so happy because they feel the music, what I have been doing has enhanced, you know if it’s playing for a certain deity that it has really enhanced they © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
being practitioners it has enhanced the music to who they are acknowledging. But it’s interesting, these things you do.
